notes: Capt. Frank Lillyman of the 101st Airborne is the first American paratrooper on the ground, marking drop zones. Times in this file are Normandy local time.
Six British gliders under Maj. John Howard land beside the bridges over the Caen Canal and the River Orne. The canal bridge will be known as Pegasus Bridge.
The main body of the British 6th Airborne Division parachutes east of the Orne.
British airborne troops capture the Merville gun battery before it can shell the invasion beaches.
1st Lt. Richard Winters and a small band of the 101st attack a German battery firing on Utah Beach.
First waves touch Utah and Omaha at 06:30. At Utah, the current sets the 4th Division down more than a mile from its aim. At Omaha, the 1st and 29th Divisions land into heavy fire.
U.S. Army Rangers start the climb to the guns said to command both American beaches.
British troops begin landing at Gold and Sword beaches.
Canadian troops begin landing at Juno Beach.
Navy beachmasters suspend vehicle landings on Omaha. Lt. Gen. Omar Bradley weighs whether the follow-on waves can keep coming in.
Allied warships are on their marks off the coast, waiting for dawn.
The fleet opens fire on the coastal batteries and beach defenses.
About 270 B-26 Marauders drop 4,404 bombs along the Norman coast, flying beneath the overcast.
The destroyer USS Corry explodes off Utah Beach. The crew abandons ship within minutes.
